Withdrawal follows verified decommissioning and proceeds in phases. It is sequenced and reciprocal. Each step rests on the successful completion of the one before it. While it has reaffirmed that framework, important questions of implementation still remain open. Nothing in the roadmap, Madam President, asks Palestinians to relinquish their rights and their aspirations. The credible pathway to a political horizon is in the comprehensive plan, and it is reaffirmed in the roadmap. Madam President, an agreed document on disarmament does not immediately mean a disarmed Gaza. But no one should understate that what was achieved in the roadmap contains three things that did not exist at any point in time before us. First is acceptance. Hamas and the factions have accepted in public the comprehensive plan and the framework requiring their complete demilitarization and a complete handover of governance in Gaza, civilian and security, direct and indirect. The second is agreement on a key principle, one authority, one law, one weapon. The claim of every armed movement around the world rests on the right to hold weapons outside the legitimate authority. This principle requires that the factions relinquish that claim. Thirdly is the architecture. Progress is performance-based, not calendar-based. A phase opens only when the previous one has been certified as completed. That constrains all sites and all must understand it as such. Our approach in the implementation phase will be to trust nothing and verify everything. What has been agreed on paper will matter only if it is translated into verified action. Madam President, as you and the rest of the Council know quite well from your own experience, Much of the debate about Gaza is a debate about either weapons or the miserable conditions in the strip. This is understandable. But Gaza's crisis has never been only a security or a humanitarian problem. It has always been a political and a governance problem. For nearly 20 years, political authority, military power and public administration were fused into the hands of a militant faction that built up its arsenal and capabilities. Israel dealt with it as a security problem to be managed rather than resolved, an approach that neither disarmed that faction nor displaced it, but it preserved it as the only address for everyone in Gaza. The price paid for that status quo of two decades was paid in blood. Repeated wars, economic collapse, isolation, and immense suffering for both Israelis and Palestinians. That is why the alternative to armed rule cannot be built in the absence of a legitimate civilian authority. Under UN Security Council Resolution 2803, the National Committee, the NCAC, was constituted in January. Madam President, before I turn to the humanitarian situation, Let me say what no indicator can actually carry. Next to them live the families in Israel who lost their loved ones in the massacre of October 7th. Grief in this conflict has never respected and will never respect lines, fences, borders, or walls. Nothing said in this chamber will restore what has been lost by the people. Unfortunately, vengeance will only beget more vengeance, and the cycle of pain will never end. However, what we owe all these families is not yet another expression of sympathy, but relief, security, and a way out of the cycle of pain and suffering. A year ago, almost to this day, in fact, the famine review committee confirmed famine in Gaza, the first time ever recorded in the region. The Board of Peace urges the State of Israel to allow better shelter into the Strip for dignity, for health, and for safety. The International Stabilization Force, Madam President, continues also to generate under the command of US Major General Jasper Jeffers. Sites are being prepared, and further countries are joining those that have stepped forward. I thank them and I renew my appeal for continued contributions. We will track implementation of the commitments by the parties and progress in the handover of governance responsibility to the National Committee. This is a critical tool to build confidence, track progress, and identify obstacles early enough to address them. Alongside, we're also implementing a very much needed deconfliction arrangement, a coordination cell and a liaison through which emerging threats on the ground can be raised and dealt with before they escalate. In our last meeting with the Prime Minister of Israel, we went through his government's concerns one by one and narrowed the areas that still require technical work. We reaffirmed a shared objective, a demilitarized Gaza that can never again pose a threat. Another winter is coming for people living in rubble and in tents. ceasefires that deliver nothing visible are not sustained by patience they are only exhausted by it madam president none of this is an argument for stopping it is an argument for knowing exactly what comes next three things must be in place for the process to move forward the ISF needs to be able to deploy Israel's undertakings under the Shamal Sheikh protocol need to be implemented and Hamas and Hamas must adhere to its commitments it is then that we can begin in those areas that conditions are best. But in UNICEF's words, quote, children's nutrition improves when aid and commercial supplies reach them, end quote. But Madam President, frankly, after hearing Ms. Rayburn's briefing, it's quite disturbing to hear a representative of civil society at this council ignore UN reports including by the Commission of inquiry frankly no friend of Israel over the years with repeated incredible reports of torture by Hamas not a word from Miss Rayburn or civil society briefing not a word on the kneecapping of Palestinians who recently dared to step out and protest Hamas's rule not a word of other reports on Hamas using hospitals as human shields, building tunnels and command centers under schools. You don't see their leadership starving. You don't see their wives who are carrying Birkin bags on camera. They're not starving. So I would encourage everyone to reread, I'll encourage your civil society briefers to read all of resolution 2803 debated extensively, but passed by this council without opposition, including the annex, which is the only UN document that says no annexation at the same time says there is a pathway to a two state with reform. finally through this council just in the last year. And the progress that we've made is something I do think to be applauded, but realistically evaluated. And that is a result of the work that many people have done to bring calm to Gaza. It'd be nice if we have briefers here that actually say Hamas and mention these terrorists. and will continue to call on support for President Trump's comprehensive plan that was endorsed by this council and has established the international stabilization force through resolution 2803. Now, it shouldn't surprise anyone in this room that Hamas itself has committed to disarm twice now actually, first In October of 2025, following the president's peace plan and again just a few weeks ago when it accepted the 15 point action roadmap, actionable roadmap laid out by the board of peace to implement the plan. Obviously there are skeptics, we hear them. We all know what kind of organization that we're dealing with. Hamas is a terrorist group responsible for horrific acts of violence against Americans, against Israelis, against the people of Gaza and the rest of the world. And so believe me when I say that we will judge Hamas by what it does, not only by what it says, but let's also remember something else. The skeptics said the hostages would never come home, and certainly not all of them, including sadly the dead. They did come home, each and every one. We'll see. The thing is, we've heard the term impossible before. the president and his team have made a habit of proving conventional wisdom wrong the ISF the international stabilization force is one example for years this Council debated has debated the issue of Gaza during the debate over 2803 we said repeatedly there are two choices Hamas rules or the IDF occupies or work with us on a third way I hear of lot of critics as the high representative said, hand-wringing and criticizing, but I don't hear a lot of alternative credible plans. Now, for the first time, troops and personnel from partner nations are scheduled to arrive to keep the peace. Tactical vehicles are already at the ISF logistics base. Countries as far as Uganda, Morocco, Kazakhstan have offered thousands of troops to this effort. No, they are not moving as quickly as we would like, but they are moving. And yes, The disarmament of Hamas must and will be closely scrutinized. It must be verified by objective parties. Nothing and not one thing will be taken on trust. But let's not have small ambitions here. With a verified process, we have the potential to unlock a future for the people of Gaza, free from Hamas, free from suffering under terrorists that raped and pillaged them for a generation. And once Hamas demonstrates full compliance with our commitments, Israel will begin its phased and eventually complete withdrawal from the Gaza Strip. So think of those words from the comprehensive plan to end the war of Gaza again. Remember the council's pledge, Gaza cannot sustainably rebuild while Hamas retains the ability to plunge it back into war. We will be frozen in a cycle of humanitarian aid rather than rebuilding until Hamas disarms and demilitarize. So colleagues, let's sum this up. Last fall, war, hostages, suffering. And now, less than a year later, after the passage of 2803, there are no hostages in Gaza. Aid by the UN's own figures and report are reaching those in need, not enough, but far more than it was. the IDF is pulling back and the NCAG is authorized to move in. So President Trump's peace plan, the 15 now the 15 point roadmap are our best hope for peace in Gaza. Let's please put politics and agendas aside. Let's support this new way. And let's realize a better future for that young girl and UNICEF's recent report. I thank you, Madam President.
And I thank the representative of the United States for the statement. I now give the floor to the representative of France.

Thank you, Madam President. France and its European partners will remain sanctions have been adopted against the responsible entities and individuals and new ones could also be adopted. We call upon Israel to cease these unacceptable attacks and to respect UN immunities and privileges. Lastly, it is urgent that Israel transfer to the Palestinian Authority the tax revenues due to it and that it restore banking links in the long term. If it doesn't do this, the ability of the Palestinian Authority to provide essential services to its population and to implement the necessary reforms would be compromised. madam president the untenable situation in gaza and in the west bank is compromising the prospects provided by the ceasefire agreement the peace plan and resolution two thousand and eight three this situation is jeopardising the two state solution and regional stability it is for this council to preserve this political prospect and to guarantee the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people and the security of Israel. France will continue to work to this end in accordance with the New York Declaration. Thank you.
I thank the representative of France for the statement and I now give the floor to the representative of China.

Madam President, I thank acting special coordinator Alaa Akbarov. Mr. Mladenov and Ms. Rabben for their briefings. The facts are very clear the crux of the unrealized lasting peace in Gaza is the lack of political will to achieve peace and the biggest obstacle is the dangerous attempt to deliberately prolong the hostilities we urge relevant parties particularly Israel to sincerely and fully implement the ceasefire agreement and take positive steps towards lasting peace countries with significant influence on the parties should take an impartial position and make concrete efforts to advance the Middle East peace process the international community especially the Security Council must earnestly shoulder its responsibility to protect civilians in Gaza ensure the delivery of humanitarian aid and prevent an even more severe humanitarian disaster second We need to stop acts of violence and annexation and ease tensions in the West Bank. The security situation in the West Bank is becoming increasingly precarious and incidents of violence against Palestinian civilians are appalling. All settlement activities are in violation of international law and Security Council resolutions and must cease immediately. We urge Israel to fulfill its obligation as occupier and curb settler violence rather than tacitly condone it. Economic conditions in the West Bank continue to deteriorate. Israel should return promptly the withheld tax revenues and lift undue restrictions on the movement of people and goods. Yesterday, Israel again furthered its strangulation of the UNRWA, forcibly entering and occupying the Qalandia Training Center. China expresses grave concerns over the incident and urges Israel to respect UNRWA's privileges, immunities, and normal operation. Third, We must defend international fairness and justice and advance implementation of the two-state solution. The fundamental way to resolve the Palestinian-Israeli question is to stay committed to a political settlement and to the two-state solution as the right way to go, resume peace talks between Palestinians and Israelis, and to achieve an independent Palestinian statehood at an early date, as well as a harmonious coexistence of the Arab and Jewish nations. However, we have heard ongoing voices that reject and deny the two-state solution and are deeply concerned. Palestine is the homeland of all Palestinians. Governance in the West Bank and post-war reconstruction in Gaza must be conducted in line with the principle of Palestinians governing Palestine. The international community should, on the basis of international law and aimed at both symptoms and root causes, take practical actions to support the just cause of the Palestinian people in pursuit of their legitimate national interests and in and rights, reject any unilateral action that undermine the foundation of the two-state solution, and promote a comprehensive, just, and lasting solution to the Palestinian question at an early date. The Palestinian leaders' legitimate right to attend UNGA general debate should be safeguarded. President, the question of Palestine has always been at the heart of the Middle East issue. It must not be marginalized or instrumentalized. Palestinian people must not become victims of geopolitical contest. The Palestinian question has been on the UN agenda for more than 70 years, and its solution is long overdue. China stands ready to work with the international community to jointly push for an end of hostilities, ease the humanitarian disaster and implement the two-state solution, thereby making greater contribution to an early end to suffering of the Palestinian people and achieving lasting peace and stability in Middle East. Thank you, President.
The representative of China for the statement. And I now give the floor to the representative of Pakistan.

Thank you, Madam President. We thank acting special coordinator Ramiz Alakbarov and high representative Nikolai Mladenov for their comprehensive briefings. And we also take good note of the statement by Ms. Rayburn particularly including her reminder to this Council regarding its responsibilities under the UN Charter. As we have heard today, the situation in the occupied Palestinian territory is at a critical inflection point. We are witnessing two dangerous and mutually reinforcing trends. First, systematic violations of international law continue with impunity. Second, deliberate illegal actions on the ground are undermining the territorial and political foundations of a viable future Palestinian state and linked with that, the prospects of lasting peace. Together, these actions by the occupying power are prolonging the present crisis and deepening humanitarian suffering. Despite the clear position of this council and repeated calls for their secession, Israel's illegal settlement activities continue unabated. The advancement of the E1 settlement project, which would effectively sever the West Bank, is particularly alarming. Beyond threatening the territorial contiguity of a future Palestinian state, the project places thousands of Palestinians at risk of forcible displacement. The foreign ministers of Group of Eight Arab Islamic countries, including Pakistan, have unequivocally condemned Israel's settlement policies and categorically rejected the E1 plan and called it a dangerous escalation. Settler violence has also reached alarming levels. The UN recorded approximately 190 attacks per month in early 2026, which is unacceptable and warrants urgent action. The continued withholding of around $6 billion in Palestinian clearance revenue is undermining the financial position of the Palestinian Authority. and its ability to provide essential services. These revenues must be released without delay. Madam President, the situation in Gaza remains equally grave, as testified by the briefers. Despite the ceasefire and the positive diplomatic developments, Palestinians continue to face death, destruction, and severe humanitarian hardship. Since the announcement of ceasefire, more than 1,200 Palestinians have been killed. Israeli violations have continued, including repeated, unjustified, and highly indiscriminate attacks on civilian infrastructure, while the humanitarian situation remains extremely fragile. So under the circumstances, there is a valid question. If the ceasefire is holding, as we are being told, then how are strikes continuing and civilians being killed? It must be underlined that ceasefire was the first, most essential step of the plan. It must be fully respected and ceasefire as noted by Mr. Mladenov, must deliver for the people. There are nevertheless positive developments under President Trump's comprehensive plan for Gaza, endorsed by the UN Security Council Resolution 2803 and subsequent actions by the Board of Peace. notable efforts have been undertaken to advance peace and take the process forward. However, despite the mediation by the United States, Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey, Israel's continued military escalation and rejection of the roadmap threatened to derail this diplomatic process and undermine the prospects for peace. And President, we are also deeply concerned by the unauthorized entries by Israeli authorities into UNRWA's premises in occupied East Jerusalem. The forcible entry into the Qalandia training center yesterday is particularly troubling. UN facilities and personnel must be respected and protected, and their privileges and immunities must be upheld in accordance with international law and the UN charter. I must note that all members around this table, all members of the council have rejected annexation. So we must therefore ensure that we stop all steps that are moving in that direction. Second, the Gaza peace plan and resolution 2803 must be implemented fully and in good faith, starting with full enforcement of the ceasefire, and its proper verification. Three, those with influence must use their diplomatic and economic leverage to enforce compliance with international law and Security Council resolutions. Fourth, to ensure accountability for all violations of international law and international humanitarian law in the occupied Palestinian territory, including war crimes and other grave violations. Mr. Mladenov rightly referred to real human, personal, and painful tragedy behind the numbers and figures that we often hear. That is the tragedy endured by the besieged populations, the Palestinians, under a brutal occupation that has continued for decades. And that is the root cause of the problem. And it is that illegal occupation that must be vacated in the interest of durable peace and stability in the region, and which is a shared objective of this council and the wider international community. Pakistan's solidarity with the Palestinian people remains firm. We stand with them in their legitimate struggle for dignity, justice, and self-determination. The only viable path to peace for all people in the region is a just comprehensive peace based on UN Security Council resolutions and international legitimacy with the establishment of an independent sovereign Palestinian state on pre-1967 borders and Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital. I thank you.
Thank the representative of Pakistan for its statement, and I now give the floor to the representative of Bahrain.

Thank you, Representative of Bahrain for the statement. And I now give the floor to the Representative of Latvia.

Thank you, Madam President. I thank Acting Special Coordinator, Mr. Ramez Alaghbarah for his informative briefing. And I welcome the Board of Peace High Representative for Gaza, Mr. Nikolay Mladenov to this meeting and thank him for the comprehensive briefing. I also thank the Executive Director of the Association of International Development Agencies, Ms. Athena Rayburn, for her contribution to the discussion. Since the announcement of the cessation of hostilities, more than 1,200 Palestinians have been killed and over 4,000 injured. The rhetoric of annexation and statements calling for targeted killings of Palestinians expressed by some Israeli politicians are unacceptable. Further constructive steps are needed to advance the comprehensive plan and prevent resurgence of violence in Gaza. There is no future for non-state armed groups and terrorism in Gaza. We once again underline that complete disarmament of Hamas and its relinquishing of power are imperative. Concurrently, the deployment of the international stabilization force and the withdrawal of the IDF must take place, as outlined by Mr. Mladenov. The early involvement of the Palestinian Authority, alongside its ongoing reform efforts and preparations for the upcoming elections, would lay the foundation for future self-sustaining governance in Gaza. Second, three months before the anniversary of the adoption of Resolution 2803, the humanitarian situation in Gaza remains appalling. Conditions are continuously critical across multiple sectors with severe water insecurity depriving civilians of adequate access to safe drinking water and the water needed for basic hygiene and sanitation. These conditions are compounding already grave public health risks amid disrupted health services, damage to and attacks on healthcare facilities and personnel, and persistent shortages of essential medicines, medical supplies and equipment. Repeated displacement continues to expose civilians to increasingly precarious conditions. And as we heard, there is an urgent need for basic shelter assistance and other vital relief to meet the needs of displaced families, especially ahead of the winter. Sustained, safe and predictable humanitarian access remains essential to an effective response and must be facilitated without conditions in accordance with international humanitarian law and humanitarian principles. International humanitarian organisations, including UN agencies and international NGOs, continue to play a critical role in delivering life-saving assistance despite severe operational constraints, and their work must not be hindered. Third, the international community, including this Chamber, has repeatedly opposed the entrenching annexation of the West Bank. Today, we note with regret that the expansion of illegal Israeli settlements, including in the E1 area, continues. Increased settler attacks and harassment, movement restrictions, and demolition of property and infrastructure contribute to the forced displacement of Palestinians and fuel the vicious cycle of vengeance and radicalization. We urge Israel to address the situation in full respect of international law and commitments, including Security Council Resolution 2334, as well as all previous arrangements to which it has pledged itself. The withheld Palestinian tax revenues must be released without delay. Attacks against Israeli civilians, incitement to violence and all forms of terrorism are equally unacceptable, and the Palestinian Authority must fulfil its commitments to pursue meaningful comprehensive reforms. This includes strengthening governance and accountability, addressing radicalisation, including education in line with UNESCO standards, and reforming the payment system for families of prisoners. Madam President, it is essential that the comprehensive plan delivers the expected results. Neither Israeli security concerns nor the legitimate aspirations of the Palestinians can be realised amidst the risk of reigniting yet another devastating escalation. A political perspective encompassing Gaza and the West Bank is the only way to achieve long-term stability. It is crucial to continue and reinforce international engagement towards peaceful coexistence through the two-state solution, in line with the relevant Security Council resolutions and the New York Declaration, and Latvia reaffirms its very firm commitment to the shared objective of peace and stability in the region. I thank you.

We regret that some of those present in the Security Council chamber for whatever reason continue to remain silent about the real picture what's happening around Gaza perhaps they should listen to the voices of reason from those countries which are also members of the board of Peace they were also referred to today specifically we refer to the latest statement by the foreign ministers of the Arab Muslim group of eight of 16th of August who collectively condemned Israel's position and placed full responsibility on West Jerusalem for undermining efforts to improve the situation both in Gaza and in the rest of the OPT, specifically the West Bank. There, the Israeli authorities are consistently pursuing a policy of strengthening their administrative and legal control contrary to the provisions of Resolution 2334. The settlement activity of Netanyahu's government is breaking all records, and we are being regularly informed about this by Mr. Al-Akbarov.
